31153.notes: Nebraska tax-lien (certificate) county — you buy the lien, not the property. Sarpy County Treasurer holds the annual public tax sale on the first Monday in March (2026 cycle: March 2, 2026, 9:00 a.m., Sarpy County Boardroom, 1210 Golden Gate Dr, Papillion). Check-in 8:30 a.m. After the public sale, unsold certificates typically move to private sale. Certificates earn statutory interest; investor must pursue tax deed/foreclosure after the statutory waiting period (generally three years under Neb. Rev. Stat. Ch. 77) if unredeemed — treasurer does not automatically issue marketable title. Sold AS IS; no ownership rights during the certificate period.
31153.auctionFormat: In-person (public certificate auction; private sale thereafter)

auctionPlatform.label: Sarpy County Treasurer — Public Tax Sale

31153.auctionFrequency: Annually first Monday in March (e.g. March 2, 2026); private sale of unsold certificates after public sale closes
31153.depositRules: Non-refundable $25 registration fee per entity/bidder (due by the Friday before sale — e.g. Feb 27, 2026 for the March 2026 cycle; email taxsale@sarpy.gov or register in office). $25 non-refundable fee per tax certificate purchased. Assignment/tax-deed fees $20 each plus notary if required. Bring W-9; one person may represent multiple entities (each pays $25). Payment of taxes bid + fees at purchase — confirm current forms of funds on the treasurer packet.

taxCollector.label: Sarpy County Treasurer — Tax Sale

clerkOfCourt.label: Sarpy County Register of Deeds / Clerk (records tax deeds)

31153.survivingLiens: A Nebraska tax sale certificate is a lien only. Mortgages, HOA, municipal, and other liens generally remain until a proper tax-deed foreclosure clears them. Federal tax liens can survive. Always run full title and follow Neb. Rev. Stat. Ch. 77 notice/foreclosure timelines — missed statutory deadlines can extinguish the certificate investment.
31153.quietTitle: After statutory waiting period, purchaser typically needs judicial foreclosure or treasurer’s deed process plus quiet title for insurable marketable title. Title companies rarely insure on certificate alone.

42019.notes: Pennsylvania Real Estate Tax Sale Law (RETSL / 72 P.S. §5860) county. Butler County Tax Claim Bureau runs three sequential sale types: (1) Upset Sale — second Monday of September each year for parcels ~2+ years delinquent (e.g. Sept 8, 2025, 6:00 p.m., Government Center Annex); purchaser takes subject to most mortgages/liens; (2) Judicial Sale — free-and-clear style after proper lienholder notice, opening at costs + deed/transfer fees; (3) Repository List — sealed bids to taxing districts for unsold parcels. No post-Upset owner redemption after sale per published notice. Buyer-beware title research mandatory.

42019.auctionFrequency: Upset Sale annually second Monday in September; Judicial Sales as scheduled (multiple per year historically); Repository continuous by bid form
42019.depositRules: Bidder registration required ~10 days prior to Upset Sale with non-refundable $20 fee (confirm current form on Tax Claim Bureau page). Upset Sale terms: certified funds; all sales final; owners may not redeem after 10:00 a.m. sale day. Purchaser receives deed in fee simple from Bureau as trustee grantor and pays transfer taxes/recording. Judicial Sale: start at costs + recording/transfer; free and clear if parties properly notified. Title search strongly recommended — PA/U.S. case law warns Upset may not divest all mortgages/judgments.

taxCollector.label: Butler County Tax Claim Bureau

clerkOfCourt.label: Butler County Prothonotary / Recorder of Deeds

42019.survivingLiens: Upset Sale: purchaser often remains responsible for mortgages, judgments, and other liens of record — sale primarily recovers delinquent taxes. 42019.quietTitle: Especially after Upset Sale, quiet title (or reliance on Judicial/Repository free-and-clear path) is commonly needed for insurable title. Do not assume Upset deed is clear.

26093.notes: Michigan tax-deed (PA 123 of 1999) county — not a lien-certificate state. Delinquent taxes forfeit to the county treasurer in year two; if unpaid by March 31 of the third year, Circuit Court enters foreclosure and clear title passes to the Foreclosing Governmental Unit (typically county treasurer) April 1. Public auction of foreclosed parcels follows in summer (commonly July; Michigan Public Land Auction / tax-sale.info is the statewide auction platform used by many counties including Livingston). After foreclosure, prior owner cannot redeem. Occupied homes and vacant land both appear; sold AS IS.
